Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A market analysis published by Monex on February 8, 2024, suggested that platinum prices, having given back their December 2023 gains, were testing the lows of 2023.; The forecast indicated a likely consolidation around $900 in the near term; with a potential drop towards $800 in the event of a broad market sell-off. <2> CPM Group, in a report published by Monex, forecast that platinum prices would average $962.40 in 2024; a slight decrease of 0.9% from the previous year. <3> A report on U.S. auto sales for the third quarter of 2023, published on December 17, 2023, indicated a mixed recovery for the automotive sector. The data showed a significant 16% increase in sales compared to the third quarter of 2022. However, these sales figures were still 8% below the pre-pandemic levels of Q3 2019. This uneven recovery in the automotive industry, a key consumer of platinum for catalytic converters, provided a complex demand signal for the metal. <4> In a report released on December 14, 2023, the World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) highlighted the significant economic strain on platinum mining operations due to a decline of over 40% in the Platinum Group Metals (PGMs) basket price over the preceding year. [3] This price drop has jeopardized the financial viability of a substantial portion of the primary platinum supply. The WPIC estimated that approximately 25% of PGM mine production was operating with negative cash margins at the prevailing spot basket price. [3] <5> On December 13, 2023, Lifezone Metals Limited announced the signing of a term sheet with a subsidiary of Glencore plc to establish a joint venture based in the United States. The partnership aims to recycle platinum, palladium, and rhodium (collectively known as platinum group metals or PGMs) from used automotive catalytic converters. The project will utilize Lifezone Metals' proprietary hydrometallurgical technology, known as Hydromet, which is intended to be a cleaner and more efficient extraction method than traditional smelting and refining. The collaboration is structured in two phases, with the initial phase involving a confirmatory pilot program and a feasibility study at Lifezone Metals' labs in Perth, Australia, to determine the project's economic viability and technical specifications before proceeding to the construction of a commercial-scale facility. <6> A Monex report published in December 2023 projected that platinum prices would likely trade sideways, predominantly within a range of $850 to $950 per ounce in the near future. [1] The analysis noted that after hitting a one-year low in the first half of November 2023, prices recovered but were unable to sustain a position above the $950 resistance level. [1] The report also mentioned that prices could occasionally move outside this primary range, potentially dropping to $800 or rising to $1,000. [1] <7> The World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) released its Platinum Quarterly report for the third quarter of 2023, confirming a third consecutive quarterly market deficit of 40,000 ounces. [2] The report, published on November 21, 2023, detailed that total platinum supply for Q3 2023 was 1,770 koz, a 2% decrease year-on-year, while total demand was a robust 1,810 koz, representing a 24% increase compared to the same period in the previous year. [2] For the full year 2023, the WPIC revised its forecast to a record deficit of 1,071,000 ounces. This updated forecast was based on an expected 3% decline in total annual supply to 7,079 koz and a significant 26% increase in annual demand to 8,150 koz. [2, 3] The strong growth in demand was largely attributed to a 14% jump in automotive demand and substantial capacity expansions in the glass and chemical industrial sectors. [3] <8> In its third-quarter results announcement on November 2, 2023, Sibanye-Stillwater reported a significant year-on-year decline in the adjusted Ebitda for its US Stillwater Mine, which fell to R397 million ($21 million) from R895 million ($52 million). [1] The company attributed the drop to several factors, including persistent inflation, skills shortages leading to staff departures, and an unexpectedly sharp and rapid decline in palladium prices. These challenges resulted in higher-than-planned costs and a reliance on expensive contractors. [1] In response to these elevated costs, CEO Neal Froneman indicated that the company was considering further repositioning of its US operations. <9> A report on U.S. Mint bullion coin sales for the third quarter of 2023 confirmed that no American Eagle 1-ounce platinum bullion coins were sold in July, August, or September of that year. The total sales for the year through the end of September remained unchanged at 12,700 coins. All of these sales occurred between March and June 2023. <10> On September 29, 2023, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) released data for August 2023, revealing that the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index had increased by 3.5% from the same month in the previous year. This index is a significant measure of inflation monitored by the Federal Reserve. The data also indicated a more subdued rise in core PCE, which excludes food and energy, with an increase of 0.1% for the month. This mixed inflation data provides crucial context for the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions, which can subsequently affect investor outlook on assets like precious metals.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A June 2024 analysis of the platinum market revealed that prices had increased in May, mirroring a trend in other precious metals. On May 20, 2024, platinum's intraday high reached $1,105, a peak not seen since May of the previous year. [5] Following this high, prices declined, nearing the $1,000 mark by June 6, 2024. [5] <2> In May 2024, the platinum market experienced a significant price surge, with the spot price exceeding $1,090 on Monday, May 20th. This increase was part of an exceptional month for the precious metal, which saw its value climb throughout April and May. The primary drivers behind the rally were a forecasted record supply deficit for 2024, geopolitical tensions, and speculation about potential interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. These factors also contributed to positive price movements in other precious metals like gold and silver. The World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) confirmed expectations of a significant supply deficit for the year, underscoring the market's fundamental support for higher prices. <3> A monthly market report for April 2024 indicated a volatile month for platinum prices, with gains made in the first half being entirely lost in the second half. [1] This movement was part of a broader trend of prices trading sideways, largely contained within a range of $880 to $1,000 since mid-2023. [1] The report identified positive factors supporting platinum demand, including a noted slowdown in the consumer adoption of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and sustained strong demand within major commercial vehicle markets. [1] <4> An April 5, 2024, outlook on the platinum market noted that while March prices were dragged higher by rising gold prices, they remained lower than at the start of the year. The analysis concluded that without an actual drop in supply, significant price increases were unlikely. It was projected that prices would largely continue to move within the $900 to $950 range, a pattern that had been established since the beginning of March. <5> Sibanye-Stillwater announced its full-year 2023 production results, confirming that its US PGM (Platinum Group Metals) underground operations produced 427,272 2Eoz (ounces of platinum and palladium), a 1% increase compared to 2022. [2, 5] This output was in line with the company's revised guidance for the year. [2, 5] In contrast, the US PGM recycling operations experienced a significant downturn, with the total PGM ounces fed decreasing by 48% year-on-year to 310,314 3Eoz. [2, 3] The company attributed this sharp decline to a depressed market for used autocatalysts, which was caused by global economic uncertainty, recessionary concerns, and higher interest rates impacting new vehicle sales and leading to vehicles remaining in service longer. [2, 3] <6> A market analysis published by Monex on February 8, 2024, suggested that platinum prices, having given back their December 2023 gains, were testing the lows of 2023.; The forecast indicated a likely consolidation around $900 in the near term; with a potential drop towards $800 in the event of a broad market sell-off. <7> CPM Group, in a report published by Monex, forecast that platinum prices would average $962.40 in 2024; a slight decrease of 0.9% from the previous year. <8> A report on U.S. auto sales for the third quarter of 2023, published on December 17, 2023, indicated a mixed recovery for the automotive sector. The data showed a significant 16% increase in sales compared to the third quarter of 2022. However, these sales figures were still 8% below the pre-pandemic levels of Q3 2019. This uneven recovery in the automotive industry, a key consumer of platinum for catalytic converters, provided a complex demand signal for the metal. <9> In a report released on December 14, 2023, the World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) highlighted the significant economic strain on platinum mining operations due to a decline of over 40% in the Platinum Group Metals (PGMs) basket price over the preceding year. [3] This price drop has jeopardized the financial viability of a substantial portion of the primary platinum supply. The WPIC estimated that approximately 25% of PGM mine production was operating with negative cash margins at the prevailing spot basket price. [3]

More significantly, revenue from these sales grew by double digits, a trend attributed to a market shift toward higher-value platinum items. This growth was supported by targeted marketing campaigns encouraging the use of platinum as an alternative to white gold, especially as gold prices remained high. The proposal affects 35 product categories and suggests adding 14 new standards and ecolabels across new categories for healthcare, laboratories, and clothing, while also expanding the food service ware category. This shift in procurement standards could influence future demand for industrial materials, such as platinum used in healthcare and laboratory settings. <3> A market analysis report from CPM Group, published by Monex on August 9, 2024, detailed a weakening of platinum prices during July 2024. [1] This downturn broke a multi-month upward trend that had been in place since early March. [1] The report forecasts that prices are expected to continue a downward trend over the next few months. This prediction is primarily driven by mounting concerns of an economic slowdown anticipated in the second half of 2024. [1] Such a slowdown could negatively affect demand for platinum, particularly within the commercial vehicle sector, which is already showing signs of weakness. [1] <4> A weekly market analysis published on August 2, 2024, emphasized the growing importance of the hydrogen economy for future platinum demand. [1] Countries like Japan, South Korea, and Germany are leading investments in hydrogen infrastructure, with energy companies such as Shell, BP, and Total also investing billions into related projects. [1] The primary drivers for this demand are platinum's use in electrolyzers for hydrogen production and in hydrogen fuel cells for power generation. [1] The analysis concluded that this emerging use strengthens the long-term investment case for platinum, suggesting that by 2040, hydrogen-related demand could become the largest sector for the metal. [1] This movement was part of a broader trend of prices trading sideways, largely contained within a range of $880 to $1,000 since mid-2023. [1] <8> An April 5, 2024, outlook on the platinum market noted that while March prices were dragged higher by rising gold prices, they remained lower than at the start of the year. metadata.original_text: This time series records platinum USD t oz data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-02-18 to 2025-03-05. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A Nasdaq article published on January 22, 2025, presented a range of analyst forecasts for platinum prices throughout 2025. Among the predictions, UBS Group set a mid-year price target of $1,100 per ounce. In a similar vein, Heraeus Precious Metals anticipated a trading range for platinum between $850 and $1,220 per ounce. The consensus among analysts pointed to a market deficit for the third consecutive year, a factor expected to support prices. However, views on the extent of the price increase varied. CPM Group, for instance, projected a flatter trajectory, with prices potentially facing downward pressure and staying within the $900 to $1,000 range. The World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) expected overall platinum demand to remain relatively stable in 2025, with a slight decrease of 1 percent. The automotive sector is predicted to be the primary driver of demand, although the increasing market share of electric vehicles presents a long-term challenge. Conversely, demand from the jewelry sector was forecasted to see a modest increase. <2> Throughout late 2024, multiple reports detailed advancements in alternative electric vehicle battery technologies.; These advancements include technologies such as sodium-ion and solid-state batteries.; These developments signal a long-term trend. <3> In its third-quarter report released in November 2024, the World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) projected that global platinum jewelry demand would increase by 2% in 2025. The report specifically anticipated continued growth in North America, attributing this outlook to post-election sentiment in the region. <4> A Q2 2024 report from Platinum Guild International (PGI) indicated a divergence in performance for the United States platinum jewelry market. While the overall US jewelry market saw a continued decline in unit sales, PGI's strategic partners reported a 1.2% increase in platinum unit sales compared to Q2 2023. More significantly, revenue from these sales grew by double digits, a trend attributed to a market shift toward higher-value platinum items. This growth was supported by targeted marketing campaigns encouraging the use of platinum as an alternative to white gold, especially as gold prices remained high. In contrast, a separate report on PGI's partners noted a 6.8% year-over-year increase in platinum jewelry sales for the same quarter. <5> On September 10, 2024, the World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) released its Platinum Quarterly report for the second quarter of 2024, in which it revised its full-year forecast. The council projects a significant market deficit of 1,028,000 ounces for 2024. This revision is attributed to a 1% decline in total platinum supply from 2023's weak levels, down to a forecasted 7,089,000 ounces, coupled with robust demand expected to reach 8,118,000 ounces. Key drivers for demand include the automotive sector, with platinum usage predicted to grow by 1% to a seven-year high, and the industrial sector, where demand is also forecast to rise by 1% to 2,369,000 ounces. Additionally, investment demand saw a significant surge in the second quarter, reaching its highest point since the third quarter of 2020. <6> On September 10, 2024, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced a proposed update to its Recommendations of Specifications, Standards, and Ecolabels for Federal Purchasing. This initiative, the first comprehensive update in nearly a decade, aims to assist federal government buyers in selecting more sustainable and climate-friendly products by utilizing private sector standards and ecolabels. The proposal affects 35 product categories and suggests adding 14 new standards and ecolabels across new categories for healthcare, laboratories, and clothing, while also expanding the food service ware category. This shift in procurement standards could influence future demand for industrial materials, such as platinum used in healthcare and laboratory settings. <7> A market analysis report from CPM Group, published by Monex on August 9, 2024, detailed a weakening of platinum prices during July 2024. [1] This downturn broke a multi-month upward trend that had been in place since early March. [1] The report forecasts that prices are expected to continue a downward trend over the next few months. This prediction is primarily driven by mounting concerns of an economic slowdown anticipated in the second half of 2024. [1] Such a slowdown could negatively affect demand for platinum, particularly within the commercial vehicle sector, which is already showing signs of weakness. [1] <8> A weekly market analysis published on August 2, 2024, emphasized the growing importance of the hydrogen economy for future platinum demand. [1] The report stated that although the hydrogen sector is still in its infancy, significant government support and private investment are positioning it to become a major consumer of platinum. [1] Countries like Japan, South Korea, and Germany are leading investments in hydrogen infrastructure, with energy companies such as Shell, BP, and Total also investing billions into related projects. [1] The primary drivers for this demand are platinum's use in electrolyzers for hydrogen production and in hydrogen fuel cells for power generation. [1] The analysis concluded that this emerging use strengthens the long-term investment case for platinum, suggesting that by 2040, hydrogen-related demand could become the largest sector for the metal. [1] <9> A June 2024 analysis of the platinum market revealed that prices had increased in May, mirroring a trend in other precious metals. On May 20, 2024, platinum's intraday high reached $1,105, a peak not seen since May of the previous year. [5] Following this high, prices declined, nearing the $1,000 mark by June 6, 2024. [5] <10> In May 2024, the platinum market experienced a significant price surge, with the spot price exceeding $1,090 on Monday, May 20th. This increase was part of an exceptional month for the precious metal, which saw its value climb throughout April and May. The primary drivers behind the rally were a forecasted record supply deficit for 2024, geopolitical tensions, and speculation about potential interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. These factors also contributed to positive price movements in other precious metals like gold and silver. The World Platinum Investment Council (WPIC) confirmed expectations of a significant supply deficit for the year, underscoring the market's fundamental support for higher prices.
